description: Use when an alert, latency regression, workload failure, unavailable service, or other operational incident needs evidence gathering, safe remediation, verification, work-tracking follow-up, and a team notification.
planning_instructions: Investigate before changing state. For latency or availability symptoms, gather bounded metrics; for workload symptoms, gather current workload state, detailed resource conditions or events, and bounded recent logs. Run independent evidence requests in parallel.

Treat an empty metric result as unavailable evidence rather than proof of health or failure. Corroborate it with workload state, endpoints, application logs, or another independent signal before identifying a cause.

When a later action needs one identifier from a structured collection, complete collection discovery in one phase and pass the prior step's declared top-level result collection into the later phase for semantic parameter resolution. Extract and supply one concrete scalar identifier to a scalar parameter.

Prefer direct discovered evidence and action capabilities. Delegate to another agent only when the current catalog lacks a direct capability or the request needs genuinely different specialist judgment.

Before a state-changing operation, identify the exact resource and scope, inspect its current state, respect the configured approval policy, perform the smallest justified change, and poll until the intended stable state or a bounded timeout. Verify the final state with concrete evidence.

After investigation and any remediation verification, locate a recent matching operational record from memory or the discovered work-tracking system, update an open match, or create a record when no match exists. Include severity, alert fingerprint, evidence, root cause or remaining uncertainty, remediation or no-change decision, and verification. Make the team notification depend on the record action so it can use the exact returned reference and human-facing link field advertised by the current capability schema.
Treat a capability action as complete only after its returned result confirms success. Record unsuccessful, timed-out, or still-progressing actions with their observed state and attempted recovery.

For command-style results, require a zero exit code and no error output in addition to a successful transport or wrapper status. Do not claim that a change was applied when the command failed, or that verification passed when the expected observable state did not change.

When a delegated specialist already returns confirmed tracking-record and notification outcomes, reuse those results and do not create duplicate follow-up actions. Verify any delegated remediation claim against its returned command outcome and post-change evidence.

When a step consumes another step's result, declare a same-phase producer in depends_on and a prior-phase producer in implicit_deps. Reference only top-level output fields advertised by the current capability schema; pass a declared collection to semantic parameter resolution when one item must be selected.
response_instructions: Separate observed evidence from inference, state when a signal returned no data, and summarize the affected scope, root cause or remaining uncertainty, remediation or no-change decision, final verification, and exact tracking-record and notification outcomes. Never describe a failed command or unchanged verification signal as a successful remediation.
Keep the operations notification brief and human-readable while retaining decisive metric values, resource names, verification evidence, and the returned record URL.
tool_hints: Select direct capabilities for bounded metrics, current workload state, detailed conditions or events, and recent logs before considering a mutation or delegation.
For a justified mutation, include the narrowest state-changing capability plus bounded status or wait capabilities and final-state inspection.
Select work-tracking search and update-or-create capabilities plus a team-notification capability for the follow-up phase.

should_activate: Investigate a critical alert for an unavailable service
Find the cause of high latency and remediate it safely
Check why a Kubernetes workload is failing and document the result
should_not_activate: Test a public web page with Playwright

change_reason: Move reusable incident investigation, remediation, and follow-up procedures out of the dedicated agent prompt
